entities.summary:
**Identity & Significance**: The concept of time is a fundamental aspect of human understanding, governing our perception of the past, present, and future. It is a dimension that allows us to order events chronologically, enabling us to make sense of the world around us.

**What Happened**: The measurement of time has been a crucial factor in the development of various cultures and civilizations, with different societies adopting unique calendars and methods to track the passage of time. For example, ancient Mesopotamians used a sexagesimal system based on 60, which is still reflected in our modern clock faces. Similarly, the Mayans developed a sophisticated calendar system that incorporated interlocking cycles to measure time.

**Legacy & Consequence**: The concept of time has had a profound impact on human society, influencing everything from scientific inquiry and philosophical debates to artistic expression and cultural practices. The development of modern chronochemistry has allowed us to study the age of materials in detail, while the notion of time zones has facilitated global communication and commerce.

**The Power of Time**: 'Time is what we want most, yet what we use worst,' said William Penn. This poignant observation highlights the dual nature of time – a resource we strive for yet squander through our daily routines.
